subtopics.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness (3 of 4)

outcomes.text: Designs and implements a strength and conditioning program that develops balance in opposing muscle groups (agonist/antagonist) and supports a healthy, active lifestyle.
Relates physiological responses to individual levels of fitness.
Identifies the different energy systems used in a selected physical activity (e.g., adenosine triphosphate and phosphocreatine, anaerobic glycolysis, aerobic).

Identifies and participates in various types of strength exercises (isometric, concentric, eccentric) and stretching exercises (Static, proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF), dynamic) for personal fitness development (e.g., strength, endurance, range of motion).

subtopics.title: The physically literate individual demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness (4 of 4)

outcomes.text: Creates and utilizes an activity plan for strength and stretching for personal fitness development.
Calculates target heart rate and applies heart rate information to a personal fitness plan.
Adjusts pacing to keep heart rate in the target zone, using available technology (e.g., pedometer, heart rate monitor), to self-monitor aerobic intensity.
Analyzes the components of skill-related fitness in relation to life and career goals, and designs an appropriate fitness program for those goals.

outcomes.text: Applies effective self-management skills to analyze barriers and modify physical activity patterns appropriately as needed.
Accepts differences between personal characteristics, idealized body images, and elite performance levels portrayed in various media.
Exhibits proper etiquette, respect for others and teamwork while engaging in physical activity.
Exhibits the fundamentals of good sportsmanship.
Examines moral and ethical conduct in specific competitive situations (e.g., intentional fouls, performance-enhancing substances, gambling, current events in sport).

Assumes a leadership role (e.g., task or group leader, referee, coach) in a physical activity setting.
Solves problems and thinks critically in physical activity settings, both as an individual and in groups.
Accepts others' ideas, cultural diversity and body types by engaging in cooperative and collaborative movement projects.
Applies best practices for participating safely in physical activity. (e.g., injury prevention, proper alignment, hydration, use of equipment, implementation of rules, sun protection).
